question: The Indus River system includes all of the following rivers EXCEPT:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Godavari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indus River system consists of the rivers Indus, Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej, which mostly flow through the northern regions of India and Pakistan.
 
• The Godavari is not part of the Indus River system; it is India's second-longest river and flows primarily through central and southern India.
 
• The Godavari originates from Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra and empties into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The Indus River system is governed by the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 between India and Pakistan, focusing on the allocation of the river's waters.
 
• The rivers Sutlej, Ravi, and Jhelum are key tributaries of the Indus, contributing significantly to its water flow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus River System:**

 
 
• It originates from the Tibetan Plateau near Lake Mansarovar and flows through India and Pakistan before reaching the Arabian Sea.
 
• The Indus is one of the longest rivers in the world, spanning over 3,180 km.
 
• Its tributaries include Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej, which are primarily located in northern India.
 
• The Indus Basin supports agriculture and hydroelectric projects in the region.
 
 
 
• **Godavari River:**
 
 
• The Godavari is India's second-longest river after the Ganges, with a length of about 1,465 km.
 
• It flows through Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha.
 
• It is often referred to as 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganges of the South).
 
• Major tributaries include Pranhita, Indravati, Sabari, and Manjira.
 
 
 
• **Indus Waters Treaty:**
 
 
• Signed in 1960 between India and Pakistan under the mediation of the World Bank.
 
• It divides the control of the six rivers in the Indus system; India gets the eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej), while Pakistan gets the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab).
 
• This treaty has been considered a successful example of water-sharing agreements between nations.
 
 
 
• **Significance of River Systems in India:**
 
 
• River systems in India are vital for agriculture, drinking water, and hydroelectric power generation.
 
• They play a significant role in cultural and religious practices.
 
• Proper management and conservation of river systems are crucial for sustainable development.
